A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoE checkpoint-growth study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining and growth experiments, downstream benchmark results, noise ablations, and growth-timing analyses, including detailed appendix tables.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds early-growth comparisons, routing controls, growth-order experiments, and optimizer and weight analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed procedures remain interpositional layer duplication and expert/router duplication with small Gaussian perturbations, doubling both expert count and activated experts during width growth. The additional experiments test configurations and combinations of these existing procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DCLM, FineWeb-Edu, Nemotron-CC-HQ, code, and synthetic training mixture, and evaluate MMLU and the same six QA benchmarks. The community-model norm analyses also retain their coverage. New experiments vary model configurations and training stages within this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds randomly initialized new experts to the existing width-initialization comparison. Appendix C adds top-4/128-expert and top-8/64-expert controls against joint expansion. These extend the existing growth-control comparisons while retaining the original scratch-training, stacking, and noise-scale comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed-step comparisons from 2k–8k checkpoints, growth factor k=4 with 80 layers, alternative routing configurations, and opposite growth orders at 12B, together with optimizer-state and weight-similarity measurements. The scalability description also changes 54 layers to 56 and four activated experts to six; six was already specified in v1's appendix, and these reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Substantial new analyses test the convergence boundary for interposition, norm discontinuities, larger growth factors, knowledge inheritance versus random initialization, routing alternatives, and growth-order independence. Appendix E adds gradient-direction and cumulative-update analyses. The pre-/post-norm function-preservation experiment is retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Task/checkpoint averages remain distinct from uncertainty estimates, and the new cosine-similarity analyses do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds early-checkpoint results in Tables 12–19 and findings for the new controls and orthogonality analyses; Table 8 reports cumulative-update cosine similarity declining from 0.630 to 0.418. Matched retained benchmark values remain unchanged, including the 70B accuracy of 64.17. v2 Table 38 omits 16 intermediate 17B per-task result rows present in v1 Table 23.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly defines and derives the reference compute budget F_c ≈ 6N_a(20N_a), using activated parameters to obtain approximately 5.88×10^19 FLOPs for the smaller model. This is a limited analytical addition. The growth equations and pre-/post-norm mathematics remain equivalent, and no new formal proof of growth optimality or orthogonality is supplied.

C1.justification: The checkpoint-recycling, sunk-cost, and large-scale efficiency claims are retained. v2's introduction adds a more specific claimed boundary near Chinchilla-optimal compute and explicitly claims consistent performance regardless of growth order, refining the scope of the original convergence and orthogonality claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanations for effectiveness: stacking requires repairing norm discontinuities, small noise breaks symmetry while retaining knowledge, and optimizer/update divergence supports complementary growth directions. It also adds interpretations of routing saturation and capacity–compute coupling, and connects the applicability of interposition to an observed convergence boundary.

D1.justification: Table 9 newly itemizes total, active, and core parameter counts; Appendix E explains shared-parameter alignment for the new diagnostics. However, its 36-layer description conflicts with Table 9's 40 layers. v1's statement offering supplementary code fragments and promising framework release disappears; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Switch Transformers, neural-ODE regularization, DeepNet, upcycling scaling laws, and OLMoE. It more explicitly distinguishes inherited routers and small perturbations from dense-to-MoE upcycling, while retaining the original broader research positioning.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, with substantial rewriting of the abstract, related work, methodological discussion, and scalability narrative. Contribution bullets are absorbed into the introduction, function-preservation discussion moves into the appendices, and standalone reproducibility and LLM-use statements are removed.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two-column layout, with extensively resized and regrouped figures and newly structured analytical tables. v1 Figure 5's stability panels become v2 Figure 16, while the scalability loss and accuracy displays are combined in v2 Figure 11. New boundary, routing, growth-factor, and optimization figures substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 directly tests important assumptions that v1 supported mainly through structural intuition and one sequential growth path. The convergence-boundary experiments, initialization/routing controls, and opposite-order growth tests substantially strengthen the empirical justification and practical guidance without relying on improved headline scores. Inconsistent layer descriptions and removal of the code-release statement weaken reproducibility, but do not outweigh these substantial evidential gains.
